BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says gᵉzêlâh, it means plunder, spoil, robbery. The word appears 6 times, and in Leviticus, Isaiah, and Ezekiel it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that gᵉzêlâh matters because God speaks plainly, and plain words carry real weight. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
